From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood discovery — SDK quickstart ask

Hi team — quick technical notes to complement Marissa's summary. I'll run through pragmatic options for the POC below.

1) SDK setup (local)
- Python: pip install redwood-sdk, example in quickstart uses virtualenv and an env var REDWOOD_API_KEY. Start the local sample server with `python sample_server.py --model redwood-3b` to test generation and embeddings locally (calls the hosted API by default).
- TypeScript: `npm i @redwood-inference/sdk` with a sample Next.js app in the repo. Use `NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY` for client-side samples only; server code should read from server env var.

2) Auth choices
- For the dev POC: API keys scoped to the dev environment are simplest. We'll provision a key tied to your dev workspace.
- For production: recommend OIDC + short-lived tokens (we support Keycloak / Cognito flows). We can demo token exchange in the pairing.

3) Routing & failover
- Use per-request `region` hint in the SDK to prefer a region with lower latency. We'll provide a small helper function in the repo to dynamically pick region based on client IP range.
- For graceful degradation, configure a fallback model variant (smaller quantized model) — we include examples in routing.md.

4) Structured outputs & tool calling
- Quickstart has a `tools/` folder showing function/tool calling with JSON schema validation and a simple router that maps calls to internal services.
- We'll include a sample that calls a `kb_search_tool` and then uses a reranker to reorder results before returning structured JSON.

5) Embeddings & reranker pattern
- Recommend 2-step: dense embeddings (open-embedding-1) + lightweight neural reranker on top (you can host with a smaller model on Redwood Dedicated if latency is critical).
- We'll include a script `scripts/build_index.py` and an example re-ranker flow. Cost note: embeddings billed per vector unit — I'll include estimated costs for the sample doc set.

I'd be happy to run the tech pairing and walk through local testing steps.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Thanks Tom — quick answers below and next steps. I'll add these to the MAP and share an updated copy before the call.

- IP / VPN: No VPN required for our hosted API; we can provide IP ranges for allowlisting. For Private deployments we support VPC peering.
- Embeddings billing: billed per-embedding unit (per vector). I'll include a short finance-friendly summary with example counts and cost estimates for your document set.
- Data residency: we support region pinning. For your POC we can provision US-only dev and prod spaces; I'll note this in the MAP and summary.
